def dot_product_int(a, b):
    """Compute the dot product of two integer vectors, the classic
    calculation from linear algebra. a and b are lists of ints of the
    same length (possibly empty). Walk the two lists in lockstep,
    multiply each pair of corresponding entries, and accumulate the
    products into one running total. Return sum(a[i] * b[i] for all i),
    which is 0 for empty lists. In other words, an empty pair of vectors
    contributes nothing, so the total starts and stays at zero.

    >>> dot_product_int([], [])
    0
    >>> dot_product_int([1, 2], [3, 4])
    11
    """
